testName: ICT3722 · 2023/24 Assignment 2 · verified SQL concepts practice
sourceType: Paraphrased from a marked ICT3722 Assignment 2 review. Answers are independently checked against standard Oracle/SQL behaviour.
sourceLimitations: The source is a student review rather than an official memo. Ambiguous wording from the upload is not reproduced; questions below use corrected, unambiguous SQL wording.

questions.text: Which clause can be added to an Oracle SELECT statement to lock the selected rows for a later update in the same transaction?
questions.explanation:
`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` locks the selected rows so another transaction cannot make conflicting changes while your transaction is working with them.

Student note: It is row-oriented locking of the selected result, not a command for locking one column.

questions.text: In SQL*Plus-style scripting, what is a placeholder whose value is substituted into a command before execution commonly called?
questions.explanation:
A substitution variable is replaced with a supplied value when the command/script is processed.

Student note: Substitution happens before SQL execution; bind variables work differently.

questions.text: Which command explicitly locks a table in Oracle?
questions.explanation:
Oracle provides the `LOCK TABLE` statement to obtain a table lock in a specified lock mode.

Student note: Explicit table locking is different from the row locks created by ordinary DML.

questions.text: If an INSERT row violates an enforced constraint, does Oracle normally insert the valid columns of that row and leave only the invalid value for later?
questions.explanation:
A row that violates an enforced constraint is not partly inserted. The statement fails for that row/statement according to the operation.

Student note: Relational constraints protect the row as a valid whole; Oracle does not normally keep half a row.

questions.text: What happens when a normal UPDATE statement has no WHERE clause?
options: Every row targeted by the table is updated
Only the first row is updated
questions.correctAnswer: Every row targeted by the table is updated
questions.explanation:
WHERE filters rows. Without it, the SET expression applies to every row in the target table.

Student note: This is why UPDATE and DELETE need extra care.

questions.text: How are multiple column names separated in an INSERT column list?
questions.explanation:
SQL column lists use commas, for example `INSERT INTO t (a, b, c) ...`.

Student note: The values list must line up with the column list.

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the WHERE clause in an UPDATE?
options: It is optional; without it all rows are affected
It is mandatory in every UPDATE
It specifies the column being changed
questions.correctAnswer: It is optional; without it all rows are affected
questions.explanation:
The SET clause says what to change; WHERE says which rows to change.

Student note: Optional in syntax does not mean optional in careful administration.

questions.text: Which form is valid for inserting the result of a query into a table?
options: INSERT INTO target (a,b) SELECT x,y FROM source
INSERT INTO target AS (SELECT x,y FROM source)
questions.correctAnswer: INSERT INTO target (a,b) SELECT x,y FROM source
questions.explanation:
`INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...` copies query results into the target table when columns/data types are compatible.

Student note: Do not put `AS` between the target and SELECT in this form.

questions.text: Which SQL category contains INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE?
questions.explanation:
INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE manipulate table data and are commonly grouped as Data Manipulation Language operations.

Student note: DDL changes structures; DML changes data.

questions.text: Can Oracle's SYSDATE value be used in an INSERT statement?
questions.explanation:
`SYSDATE` can be used as an expression in inserted values when the target data type is appropriate.

Student note: Date/time functions are not limited to UPDATE.

questions.text: Which command modifies existing row values?
questions.explanation:
UPDATE changes values in rows that already exist.

Student note: INSERT adds; UPDATE changes.

questions.text: Which clause of UPDATE specifies the new column values?
questions.explanation:
The SET clause contains assignments such as `SET salary = 5000`.

Student note: SET = what changes; WHERE = which rows.

questions.text: Which command makes the current transaction's changes permanent?
questions.explanation:
COMMIT ends the current transaction and makes its changes permanent/visible according to database transaction rules.

Student note: SAVEPOINT marks a point inside a transaction; it does not finish the transaction.

questions.text: Which command is designed to explicitly prevent conflicting table changes by acquiring a table lock?
questions.explanation:
`LOCK TABLE` requests an explicit table lock in Oracle.

Student note: Use explicit locking only when the transaction design genuinely needs it.
